# dist/RELEASE-v59.txt (all eight targets) stay as the records of those cuts.

                                resolved symbols out of is reset mid-build (dist/ppu-reload-check.sh added with it)
parent:        v61 (2df7b40d2a) for win64 and linux64; v59 (5c89c538b8) for the other six targets

WHAT CHANGED IN v62 -- A UNIT COMPILED FROM SOURCE IS RECOMPILED, NOT RELOADED, WHEN A UNIT IT RESOLVED
SYMBOLS OUT OF IS RESET MID-BUILD
  Reported by Lars (LazarusDeveloper) 2026-09-22: after a Lazarus source pull, "lazbuild --build-ide" died
  with EAccessViolation (exit 217) inside the compiler.  It reproduces on EVERY published compiler since
  the ctask scheduler came in -- v59, v60 and v61 all measured -- and the backtrace is always
    tderef.build <- tabstractpointerdef.buildderef <- tprocdef.buildderefimpl
      <- tstoredsymtable.buildderefimpl <- tppumodule.writeppu <- finish_unit <- continue_module
  (file:line frames from a -gl -dDEBUG_PPU_CYCLES rebuild of the published v59 whose .text is
  byte-identical to the shipped binary, so the frames describe the SHIPPED compiler).

  Mechanism, read off the scheduler trace rather than guessed:
    * editormacrolistviewer was loaded from its .ppu; sourceeditor was compiled FROM SOURCE against it.
    * Only when sourcefilemanager finished did the scheduler learn that editormacrolistviewer's
      IMPLEMENTATION uses sourcefilemanager, whose checksum had changed.  A uses cycle through an
      implementation section defers that check -- that is why this needs a real IDE-sized unit graph.
    * editormacrolistviewer was reset and recompiled from sources.  tmodule.flagdependent then flagged
      sourceeditor -- and designer, sourcefilemanager, mainbase, buildmodesmanager, projectinspector,
      debugmanager, formeditor behind it -- for a RELOAD.
    * tppumodule.reload -> re_resolve can only re-resolve DEREF TABLES.  A unit compiled from source has
      interface derefs only (getppucrc builds those); its implementation side -- the local symtables of its
      routines, inline bodies, generated code -- holds DIRECT POINTERS.  sourceeditor kept pointers into
      editormacrolistviewer's freed symtable, and writeppu walked them.
  v62 (ade0c47fc4, compiler/fmodule.pas, tmodule.flagdependent, +32): a dependent that is NOT fromppu is marked
  for a full recompile (recompile_reason rr_crcchanged, do_recompile, do_reload, ms_compile -- exactly the
  marking dependent_module_crc_mismatch already used for the checksum case), so the scheduler resets it and
  re-flags its own dependents.  Dependents loaded from a .ppu keep the reload path unchanged.

  Upstream fpc-unleashed/main (fetched 2026-09-22, merge-base d924ff6a3b) has the identical
  flagdependent/re_resolve pair, so the defect is upstream's too and there was nothing to borrow.  Upstream's
  own -dDebug41677 "INVALID RECOMPILE" assertion does NOT fire on it (measured: same AV, ierr=0).

  COMPILER BINARY ONLY.  No RTL change, no package change, no PPU FORMAT change, so every existing unit set
  stays valid: win64 units are STILL the v52 set, linux64 units are STILL the v59 set.

PLATFORMS STILL AT v59 (NOT rebuilt for this cut) -- AND WHAT THAT MEANS
  aarch64-linux, arm-linux, arm-linux-cross, i386-linux-cross, x86_64-darwin, aarch64-darwin.
  This defect is in target-independent scheduler/module code, so the published v59 compilers for these six
  targets HAVE it -- and so does every v61 and v60 binary.  They stay at v59 for the same reason as last
  cut: none has a consumer today, the incremental-build report came from a Linux host and the pointer that
  serves it is win64.  A v62 cut for any of them is one recipe run; say which.

HOW THE DEFECT WAS FOUND (cycles 1168-1169, evidence under ~/src/vibepascal-slices/ppu-av-cy1168/)
  * The report was reproduced FIRST, on the PUBLISHED v59, as a two-step rig: Lazarus 30d1cbd292 clean-built
    (278 gtk2 ppus), then "git checkout 9d49ba95ff" (Lars's tip) and "lazbuild --build-ide" -- i.e. a source
    pull over a built tree, which is the shape Lars described.  A one-step clean build never crashes.
  * Seven small unit-cycle shapes do NOT crash on v59 even under heaptrc free-fill: on a small graph the
    scheduler resets the used unit before the source dependent parses its implementation.  They DO show the
    defect in the compiler's own -vu text ("Flag for reload" of a unit being compiled from source), which is
    what dist/ppu-reload-check.sh scores -- the gate is deliberately NOT scored on rc, because on the small
    shape the defect is silent and produces correct output by luck.
  * The scheduler trace named the mechanism; upstream was checked before the fix was written.
  * The fix was verified on the full-size rig BEFORE this cut, then re-verified on the PUBLISHED bytes.

HONEST LIMITS
  1. wine is not Windows.  The win64 exe here is the same source as the linux binary the rig ran, but no
     native-Windows incremental IDE build has been done: v59 ran on native Windows (2026-09-17), v60, v61
     and v62 have not.  Lars's own retest on the shared-tree linux compiler is the practical sign-off.
  2. Six targets stay at v59 and carry the defect, by the reasoning above.
  3. The 1987-test corpus A/B scores compile status and run exit code per test.  It cannot see this defect
     at all (no test in it recompiles a unit graph mid-build); it is here to show the fix changes NOTHING
     else.  The reload gate and the Lazarus rig are the evidence for the fix itself.
  4. The gate and the rig both exercise the x86_64-linux compiler.  The win64 exe is the same source built
     for another target, not an independently measured fix.
